passages.text: EAR, in anatomy, the organ of hearing, which is divided by anatomists into the external ear, the cavity of the tympanum, and the labyrinth.

The tympanum, or drum, is a thin membrane stretched across the end of the passage; behind it lie four small bones, the malleus or hammer, the incus or anvil, the os orbiculare, and the stapes or stirrup, which convey the tremors of the membrane to the labyrinth.

The labyrinth consists of the vestibule, the three semicircular canals, and the cochlea, which is formed like the shell of a snail; and in these the soft pulp of the auditory nerve is spread out, which is the immediate organ of hearing.
The semicircular canals are thought to serve, like the cochlea, for the perception of sounds.
The Eustachian tube passes from the cavity of the tympanum to the back of the mouth, and admits air to the inner side of the drum.
The wax of the ear, which is bitter, serves to catch the dust and to keep insects from creeping into the passage.
In vertebrates the ear is the organ of hearing and of balance. In mammals it is usually described as having three parts: the outer ear, the middle ear and the inner ear.
The eardrum, or tympanic membrane, separates the outer ear from the middle ear. Three small bones, the malleus, incus and stapes, carry its vibrations to the inner ear.
The inner ear contains the cochlea, which is the organ of hearing, and the vestibular system, which senses balance and movement.
In the cochlea, hair cells turn sound vibrations into nerve signals. These signals travel along the auditory nerve to the brain.
The semicircular canals are part of the vestibular system. They are filled with fluid and sense rotation of the head, which helps the body keep its balance.
The Eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the back of the nose and throat. It keeps the air pressure equal on both sides of the eardrum.
Earwax helps clean and protect the ear canal. It traps dust and dirt and may help keep out bacteria, fungi and insects.

reasons: Rare terms appear in both: malleus, incus, stapes, cochlea, Eustachian tube.
Hearing scores well but covers sound and perception more than the organ.

alignments.label: Three parts

britannica.quote: the external ear, the cavity of the tympanum, and the labyrinth

wikipedia.quote: the outer ear, the middle ear and the inner ear

alignments.note: Change in language. The cavity of the tympanum is the middle ear and the labyrinth is the inner ear.

britannica.quote: convey the tremors of the membrane to the labyrinth

wikipedia.quote: carry its vibrations to the inner ear

alignments.label: Four or three bones
alignments.note: The count changed. Inference: the os orbiculare is now counted as part of the incus, not as a separate bone.

alignments.label: Cochlea

britannica.quote: the cochlea, which is formed like the shell of a snail

wikipedia.quote: the cochlea, which is the organ of hearing

alignments.note: Both place hearing in the cochlea.

alignments.label: Organ of hearing

britannica.quote: the soft pulp of the auditory nerve is spread out, which is the immediate organ of hearing

wikipedia.quote: hair cells turn sound vibrations into nerve signals

alignments.note: The auditory nerve is real. Today the sensing is done by hair cells, which pass signals to the nerve.

alignments.label: Semicircular canals

britannica.quote: The semicircular canals are thought to serve, like the cochlea, for the perception of sounds

alignments.note: Change in knowledge. The canals serve balance, not hearing. Flourens showed this with pigeons in the 1820s.

alignments.label: Eustachian tube

britannica.quote: admits air to the inner side of the drum

wikipedia.quote: keeps the air pressure equal on both sides of the eardrum

alignments.note: Same function. Wikipedia names the throat behind the nose, not the mouth.

alignments.label: Earwax

britannica.quote: to keep insects from creeping into the passage

wikipedia.quote: may help keep out bacteria, fungi and insects

alignments.note: Insects are still named, but cleaning and protection against infection are now the main roles.

alignments.label: Balance

wikipedia.quote: the organ of hearing and of balance

alignments.note: The 1797 entry treats the ear as an organ of hearing only.

suggestedQuestions: What did the 1797 entry think the semicircular canals do?
How many small bones did the 1797 entry find in the ear?

What did the 1797 entry think the semici.answer: It said they serve, like the cochlea, for the perception of sounds [B4]. Wikipedia says they sense rotation of the head and help keep balance [W5].

How many small bones did the 1797 entry.answer: Four: the hammer, the anvil, the os orbiculare and the stirrup [B2]. Wikipedia names three: the malleus, incus and stapes [W2].
